# Green Stars? Not Tonight!

While distant stars typically glow white, red, or blue depending on their temperature, astronomers have discovered that some dead stellar remnants called white dwarfs—the dense leftover cores of Sun-like stars—can appear surprisingly colorful, including yellow, green, cyan, pink, or purple, when trace elements from orbiting material interact with their atmospheres and shift their natural white light. Unfortunately, these exotic stellar chameleons are too faint for even the keenest stargazer to spot with the naked eye.
